scenario_result.survives: true|false|null: the organism survives the perturbation
scenario_result.feasible: true|false|null: the behaviour asked about is possible

provenance_kinds.measured: Read from a primary source that measured it in the stated organism.
provenance_kinds.measured-secondhand: A measurement, but quoted from a citing paper, review or summary rather than read in the source. Treat as provisional.
provenance_kinds.borrowed: A real measurement, used for a molecule, tissue or stage it was NOT measured in. The borrowing is the assumption.
provenance_kinds.derived: Computed from other entries here by a stated formula, adding no new empirical content.
provenance_kinds.calibrated: Set so the model reproduces one named wild-type observation. Calibration is not prediction; a calibrated quantity can never be cited as a result.
provenance_kinds.assumed: Not measured and not fetched. A placeholder. Any conclusion resting on it inherits that.

tools.name: morphogen_diffusion
tools.title: Morphogen reaction-diffusion on a fin-bud domain
tools.description: Steady-state reaction-diffusion of one morphogen on a 2D or 3D rectangular domain standing for a pectoral fin bud, with a source region (ZPA Shh or AER Fgf). Returns the concentration field, its gradient length lambda = sqrt(D/k), and the size of the region above a threshold. Diffusion constants default to FETCHED zebrafish FCS measurements; a Shh source borrows the Fgf8 coefficient because no measured zebrafish Shh value was found, and says so.

morphogen.description: fgf uses the measured Fgf8a fast-fraction coefficient. shh uses the same number, labelled borrowed. custom requires D_um2_s.

D_um2_s.description: Overrides the fetched coefficient. Labelled assumed when given.

half_life_min.description: Overrides the fetched 9 min residence time. Labelled assumed when given.

dims.description: Grid cells per axis. Axis 0 anteroposterior, axis 1 dorsoventral, axis 2 proximodistal if 3D.

source.description: Production slab: { axis, from, to, rate }.

threshold_fraction.description: Report the region above this fraction of the peak concentration.

return_field.description: Include the full concentration field. Off by default because it is large.

tools.name: protein_structure
tools.title: Protein structure from AlphaFold DB, or a variant folded with ESMFold
tools.description: Given a UniProt accession, fetches the AlphaFold DB model and reports mean pLDDT with metadata. Given a missense variant as well, folds wild type and variant with Meta public ESMFold and reports CA RMSD and both pLDDTs. Structure prediction only: it says nothing about function.

variant.description: Missense variant in the form F326L (wild-type residue, 1-based position, variant residue). Omit for the AlphaFold model alone.

fold_variant.description: Call ESMFold when a variant is given. Requires sequence length <= 400.

tools.name: physiology_chain
tools.title: Oxygen-transport physiology chain
tools.description: Wraps physiology/index.js createPhysiology: gill oxygen uptake and the downstream transport chain for a fish of a given mass in given water. The underlying module labels each of its own quantities measured, derived, tuned or assumed, and those labels are passed through unchanged.

gillArea_m2.description: Total gill area; defaults to a per-kg value from the module.

waterO2_mg_per_l.description: Defaults to air saturation at the given temperature and salinity.

tools.name: growth_trajectory
tools.title: Growth trajectory
tools.description: Wraps development/trajectory.mjs: standard length and derived quantities against age, from the growth model fitted in that module.

quantity.description: Quantity to evaluate, passed to trajectory.at(). Omit for the whole series.

SLcm.description: Standard length in cm; converted to an age if ageDays is absent.

series.description: Return this many points instead of a single evaluation.

tools.name: lean_laws_list
tools.title: List Lean-backed laws
tools.description: Every law in the versioned law registry (physical and biological), with law_id, version, kind, status, Lean theorem and the constraint ids that evaluate it. Filter by kind, status, scope substring (matches level and scope text), lawset version, or free text.

scope.description: Substring of the law level or scope, e.g. "genotype", "physiology".

lawset.description: Only laws in this lawset version, or "current".

text.description: Substring of law_id, label or statement.

tools.name: lean_law_get
tools.title: One Lean-backed law, in full
tools.description: The full registry entry for one law: statement, the Lean source text of its theorem and of the named hypotheses its signature uses, constraint lemmas, version history, sources, non-vacuity witness, and the pinned commit and content hash with a live drift flag.

version.description: A specific law version (e.g. one an older lawset pins, served from lean/registry/law-versions/). Omit for the current one.

tools.name: lean_lawset_get
tools.title: A lawset release
tools.description: A versioned set of laws (law_id, version, content hash, pinned status) as released in the registry. "current" resolves to lean/registry/lawsets/current.json.

tools.name: lean_check
tools.title: Check a design against a lawset (NOT a kernel check)
tools.description: Evaluates a resolved state/design (SI units, fields documented at the top of lean/eliminate/browser-check.mjs) against one lawset. Evaluation is the generated browser-check (floating point); law_id, version, kind and status come from the registry. Returns per-law verdicts (holds, violated, cannot-evaluate, out-of-scope, unknown-lawset) and violations [{law_id, version, kind, status, inputs, message, binding}]. Violations of non-accepted laws are advisory (binding:false). A row is out-of-scope when the law scope (taxa, life stages, ranges) excludes the design, when the design declares a claim the law does not judge (scope.applies_to / scope.excludes: an unpowered glide is not a sustained aerobic demand, so flight_mode "glide" takes C14 and E3 out of scope), or when it compares the design with the single flying-fish reference specimen and the design is not a flying fish; give taxon (e.g. "Danio rerio") and flight_mode in the design.

design.description: SI-unit spec: taxon, life_stage, flight_mode ("glide" or "powered"; or powered: false), SL_m, mass_kg, finArea_m2, CLmax, LD_max, rho, airspeed_m_s, genotype_edits, ... (alias: spec). Declaring an unpowered glide takes the aerobic-demand laws (C14, E3) out of scope instead of violating them.

spec.description: Alias of design, accepted for compatibility with the v1 lean_check.

tools.name: lean_propose
tools.title: Propose a new Lean law (local only)
tools.description: Runs lean/registry/propose.mjs on a submitted Lean statement plus metadata and returns its verdict: candidate, contested or rejected. Never auto-accepts (an "accepted" result is downgraded to candidate). Runs a Lean build, so it is not offered on the hosted HTTP server.

source.description: Lean source text, used if file is absent.

meta.description: law_id, kind, statement_en, hypotheses, sources ... as lean/registry/README.md documents.

tools.name: lean_verify
tools.title: Verify pinned Lean sources
tools.description: Re-hashes every pinned Lean module and reports drift against the registry pins, whether each named theorem still exists, whether the static /api/lean/ mirror is stale, and whether the generated browser-check lags lean/constraints.json.

tools.name: lean_source_status
tools.title: Where the Lean laws come from, and how fresh they are
tools.description: Reports the law source this server is using: "local" (the files in this deployment), "remote:mirror" (the static /api/lean/ mirror) or "remote:github" (raw lean/registry/ on a git ref), selected by LEANBIO_REMOTE. For a remote it gives the URL, the current lawset, when it was fetched and last checked, the next check (TTL), request and 304 counts, how many law files matched their lawset content_hash, and the last error or rejected (tampered or inconsistent) fetch, which never replaces the last good set. refresh:true forces a check now (at most once per 30 s).

refresh.description: Check the remote now instead of waiting for the TTL (rate-limited to once per 30 s).

tools.name: lean_changes
tools.title: What changed in the Lean lawsets
tools.description: Lawset releases newer than since_version, newest first. Each entry has the CHANGELOG prose and bullets (lean/registry/CHANGELOG.md) and a machine diff computed from the lawset pins (laws added or removed, version changes, status changes). Poll with the lawset_version you last saw; up_to_date:true means nothing newer. The same feed is static at /api/lean/changes.json and /api/lean/changes.xml (Atom).

since_version.description: A lawset version such as "1.3.0" (exclusive), or "current". Omit for every release.

tools.name: leanbio_queue
tools.title: LeanBio formalization queue
tools.description: Claims and nanopub drafts that are candidates for a LeanBio (Lean 4) statement, ordered by formalizability (theorem before named hypothesis) then belief. Excludes anything already in the law registry, anything below the queue threshold, and items a reviewer declined. Each item has its belief breakdown (E support, R contradiction, independent evidence counts), its INDRA-style relation type and its grounded entities.

min_belief.description: Only items at or above this belief

relation.description: Only this relation type, e.g. ScalingLaw, Bound, Equality, Dynamics, Inhibition

tools.name: leanbio_ground
tools.title: Ground text or an entity to ontology identifiers
tools.description: Text -> entity mentions with groundings (Gilda NER over grounding.indra.bio; zebrafish gene symbols via MyGene.info; taxa via the repo inventory and OLS4 NCBITaxon). Or entity -> one grounding decision (identifiers such as UBERON:0000151 are verified against OLS4). Each mention has status grounded | ambiguous | low-confidence | ungroundable, the best match and alternatives. Responses are cached in pipeline/leanbio/cache/.

entity.description: One entity name or identifier, instead of text

context.description: Context for an entity (e.g. "zebrafish") to pick the organism

offline.description: Answer from the cache only (no network)

tools.name: leanbio_claim
tools.title: LeanBio record for one claim
tools.description: One claim (docs/claims.json id, e.g. "maynardsmith-hitchhiking") or draft ("draft:<repo path>") -> its grounded entities, INDRA-style statement, evidence items, belief breakdown, linked Lean laws with their CURRENT registry status, queue position or the reason it is not queued, and an unsigned nanopub draft (TriG) carrying the groundings and belief.

tools.name: leanbio_personas
tools.title: Personas: who could use Lean for Bio
tools.description: Every kind of person or agent with a reason to use a formalised law registry over biology: who they are, what they do today without it, what they would ask of it, and the tools they need with each marked EXISTS (a real tool in sim-engine/contract.json or on the delphisci MCP server), PARTIAL (real but incomplete, with a note saying what it does not do) or MISSING (a proposal, defined in leanbio_tool_gap). No persona has an empty tool list. Includes AI agents doing automated science, which is what this project's own swarm is.

text.description: Only personas whose name, who, today or would_ask mention this text

needs_tool.description: Only personas who need this tool name (real or proposed)

status.description: Only personas with at least one tool at this status

brief.description: Name, who and tool statuses only

tools.name: leanbio_use_cases
tools.title: Use cases: the tool sequence for one concrete job
tools.description: One row per job somebody would come here to do, naming the question in a user's words, the ordered tool sequence that answers it TODAY with real tool names, what is missing (with the gap id), a worked example drawn from a file in this repo where one exists, and the honest limit of the answer. `answerable_today` is derived from the step statuses: "no" means a MISSING step the route cannot be walked without. Includes the uncomfortable ones: whether a published conclusion follows from its premises, what is NOT known at each scale for a gene, and open questions ranked by how decisive new evidence would be.

id.description: One use case by id, e.g. "uc-which-laws-violated"

persona.description: Only use cases for this persona id

answerable.description: Filter by whether it can be answered today

tool.description: Only use cases whose sequence names this tool

uses_gap.description: Only use cases waiting on this tool-gap id

uncomfortable.description: Only the rows that expose a gap or whose honest answer is "we do not know"

worked_only.description: Only rows with a worked example

text.description: Only use cases whose question mentions this text

tools.name: leanbio_grand_questions
tools.title: Grand questions, split into what a proof can settle and what only measurement can
tools.description: The big open questions of biology, each separated honestly into (a) the FORMALISABLE CORE, written as conditionals so the premises are visible, with the Lean declaration in this repo that proves it where one exists; (b) the EMPIRICAL REMAINDER, item by item, each with why no proof reaches it and the measurement that would; (c) what already exists here towards it, graded real / adjacent / shape-only; (d) the tools a user would need. Lean proves that a conclusion follows from stated premises; it does not adjudicate reality, and the split is the point of the document. Citations were fetched from Europe PMC or Crossref, with both sides named for the disputed questions.

disputed.description: Only the questions the literature actively disagrees about

has_repo_asset.description: Only questions where something in this repo is graded "real" towards them

core_strength.description: How much of the question the formalisable core covers

section.description: Return only one part of each entry

with_citations.description: Resolve the citation keys into full records

tools.name: leanbio_tool_gap
tools.title: Tool gap analysis, ranked by how much each gap unblocks
tools.description: The union of every MISSING reference in the personas, use cases and grand questions, deduplicated, each with a name, a signature, what it would read, an effort estimate, whether it is buildable on what we already have or needs data we do not have, the nearest existing tool, and how it could mislead if built carelessly. `unblocks` and `rank` are counted at call time from the other three documents, so a gap cannot be promoted by editing its own entry. Also serves `not_gaps`: the things deliberately absent, so a missing feature is distinguishable from an unmade decision.

kind.description: tool: a surface over data we can reach. lean-module: a Lean file to write and propose first. data: a measurement set we do not have. integration: wiring to something outside this repo.

buildable_now.description: Only gaps that are (or are not) buildable on what we already have

unblocks_persona.description: Only gaps that unblock this persona id

unblocks_question.description: Only gaps that unblock this grand-question id

tools.name: organism_create
tools.title: Create an organism document
tools.description: New organism document, EITHER from weighted parents (reference organisms or designs; weights sum to 1) OR from a taxon. A TAXON base is for an organism this engine holds no measured parameters for: it carries the taxon, which is what law scope is decided from, and every parameter is null with a reason, so any check needing a length, mass or area returns cannot-evaluate rather than a number nobody measured. Saved under sim-engine/sessions/organisms/.

taxon.description: A taxon name (scientific name, clade or common name the clade table knows) INSTEAD of parents, for an organism outside this engine's bundle.

tools.name: organism_from_blueprint
tools.title: Organism document from a blueprint (any taxon)
tools.description: Turns an organism-design blueprint into an organism document, for ANY organism. The blueprint resolves a plain-language description to an NCBI taxon and an Uberon/CL hierarchy, for any clade. What arrives here is REAL: the taxon and the ontology terms. What does not arrive is parameters -- this engine holds measured body-plan parameters only for its own teleosts -- so they are null with a reason and every dimensional check returns cannot-evaluate. The result says, per tool, what runs and what refuses. Blueprints resolving inside the held-out clade are refused.

blueprint.description: Path to a blueprint JSON (organism-design/examples/*.json) or the parsed object.

id.description: Document id; defaults to a slug of the blueprint description.

tools.name: organism_get
tools.title: Get an organism document and its STATE
tools.description: Returns the document and, at the given age and conditions, the resolved STATE with per-field provenance.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera), or an inline organism document.

ageDays.description: Age in days after hatching. Default: the reference age of the dominant parent. Ages outside the growth data are clamped and flagged.

conditions.description: Conditions: temperature_C, salinity_psu, depth_m, altitude_m, air_O2_fraction, medium. Unset values come from conditions/baseline.json.

measured.description: Optional values measured on the edited mesh by dashboard/public/blueprint3d/partedit.js measurePart: {pectoral_area_both_m2, pectoral_span_m, lifting_area_m2}. They replace the parameter-model values in STATE (kind derived).

tools.name: organism_list_parts
tools.title: Editable part hierarchy
tools.description: body -> organ system -> organ -> tissue (mesh parts from the organism manifest) plus ontology tissue/cell terms and gene symbols, with the editable params at each level and what each edit affects.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera), or an inline organism document.

tools.name: organism_edit
tools.title: Append an edit and re-check the Lean laws
tools.description: Validates the target against the manifest/ontology/gene list (unknown ids are rejected), appends the edit, resolves STATE and returns Lean verdicts plus violations (red), contested (amber) and whether the unedited base also violates each.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera), or an inline organism document.

edit.description: One edit. author is a ROLE label (human, agent:physics), never a personal identifier.

new_id.description: When editing a repository organism, save the result under this id.

ageDays.description: Age in days after hatching. Default: the reference age of the dominant parent. Ages outside the growth data are clamped and flagged.

conditions.description: Conditions: temperature_C, salinity_psu, depth_m, altitude_m, air_O2_fraction, medium. Unset values come from conditions/baseline.json.

lawset.description: Lean lawset version (default 'current'). Read from the law registry via lib/lean-source.mjs.

tools.name: scenario_list
tools.title: List scenarios
tools.description: Every scenario module in sim-engine/scenarios with params, required STATE fields, declared metrics and model card. Modules that fail the interface are listed under errors.

tools.name: scenario_run
tools.title: Run a scenario
tools.description: Run one scenario on an organism at one age. Never runs when a required STATE field is null.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera), or an inline organism document.

ageDays.description: Age in days after hatching. Default: the reference age of the dominant parent. Ages outside the growth data are clamped and flagged.

conditions.description: Conditions: temperature_C, salinity_psu, depth_m, altitude_m, air_O2_fraction, medium. Unset values come from conditions/baseline.json.

measured.description: Optional values measured on the edited mesh by dashboard/public/blueprint3d/partedit.js measurePart: {pectoral_area_both_m2, pectoral_span_m, lifting_area_m2}. They replace the parameter-model values in STATE (kind derived).

lawset.description: Lean lawset version (default 'current'). Read from the law registry via lib/lean-source.mjs.

claims.description: Assertions the Lean laws check against the scenario's own physics, labelled as claims. {ground_distance_m} and {glideDistance_m} are the STEADY DESCENT that C15 and P4b bound; {glide_total_distance_m} is the whole glide (kinetic phase included), which no theorem covers, so it is reported and never ruled on. {flight_mode: 'powered'} says the claim is level or climbing flight, which pays a sustained power (E3, C14, C16 apply); an unpowered glide never reaches those laws. Keys: ground_distance_m, glideDistance_m, mass_change, airspeed_m_s, climbRate_m_s, current_speed_m_s, body_temperature_C, depth_m, altitude_m, sustained_power_W, intake_J_per_day, glideHeight_m, wind_along_track_m_s, glide_total_distance_m, flight_mode, powerRequired_W.

tools.name: scenario_timecourse
tools.title: Run a scenario across development
tools.description: The same scenario at every developmental stage in anatomy-model/parametric/stages.json for the organism's parents: per-stage metrics, survives, limiting, Lean violations.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera), or an inline organism document.

conditions.description: Conditions: temperature_C, salinity_psu, depth_m, altitude_m, air_O2_fraction, medium. Unset values come from conditions/baseline.json.

lawset.description: Lean lawset version (default 'current'). Read from the law registry via lib/lean-source.mjs.

tools.name: optimize
tools.title: Optimise a design against a scenario metric
tools.description: Seeded random-restart hill climb over decision variables [{target,param,min,max}]. A candidate is rejected if it creates a NEW binding Lean violation (strict: any binding violation) or breaks a hard constraint; every rejection is returned with the law or constraint it broke. If no candidate is feasible the result says "no design meets the spec".

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera), or an inline organism document.

ageDays.description: Age in days after hatching. Default: the reference age of the dominant parent. Ages outside the growth data are clamped and flagged.

conditions.description: Conditions: temperature_C, salinity_psu, depth_m, altitude_m, air_O2_fraction, medium. Unset values come from conditions/baseline.json.

hard_constraints.description: Each: {scenario, metric, op:"<="|">="|"==", value, params?, ageDays?} or {scenario, survives:true} or {scenario, feasible:true} or {state_field, op, value}.

budget.description: Evaluations (default 60, max 400), including the start design.

lawset.description: Lean lawset version (default 'current'). Read from the law registry via lib/lean-source.mjs.

tolerance.description: Relative improvement over the START design a candidate must exceed (default 0.001 = 0.1 %). Below it the result is status "no improvement" and the start design is returned unchanged.

tools.name: session_open
tools.title: Open a co-design session
tools.description: Append-only JSONL log under sim-engine/sessions/. Optionally bound to a saved organism document that kind:"edit" posts modify.

organism.description: Saved organism document id (create it first).

tools.name: session_post
tools.title: Post to a co-design session
tools.description: kind 'comment' | 'finding' (one tool run: the tool, its verdict and its numbers, stored structured -- evidence, changes nothing, any role) | 'proposal' (edits + rationale + the scenario results that motivated them; validated, NOT applied; gets a proposal_id for session_decide) | 'edit' (applied at once; only for author roles starting with 'human'). author is a role label, never a personal identifier.

tool.description: finding: the tool or check that produced it, e.g. "physics_check", "lean_check", "blueprint.mjs".

verdict.description: finding: the outcome in one word as the tool itself reported it -- pass, fail, cannot-assess, out-of-scope, refused, holds, violated.

generation.description: finding: which iteration of the design this was measured on, so a log can be read as a sequence rather than a pile.

detail.description: finding: the numbers and reasons, verbatim from the tool result. Stored as given; nothing here is recomputed.

items.description: One edit. author is a ROLE label (human, agent:physics), never a personal identifier.

edits.description: Edits (author is taken from the post).

edit.description: One edit. author is a ROLE label (human, agent:physics), never a personal identifier.

evidence.description: Scenario results (or other tool results) that motivated the proposal; stored verbatim.

lawset.description: Lean lawset version (default 'current'). Read from the law registry via lib/lean-source.mjs.

tools.name: session_decide
tools.title: Approve or reject a proposal
tools.description: Applies (approve) or rejects a proposal posted to a session. decided_by_role must be a role label starting with 'human' (agents propose, humans decide). Approval applies every edit of the proposal atomically to the session's organism and records the lawset version and the Lean violations at that moment.

lawset.description: Lean lawset version (default 'current'). Read from the law registry via lib/lean-source.mjs.

tools.name: session_read
tools.title: Read a co-design session
tools.description: Every entry (or those after `since`), plus the current organism document if the session has one.

tools.name: omics_gene
tools.title: Multi-omic card for one gene
tools.description: All omics layers for one gene of the DELPHI gene universe (3,860 zebrafish genes behind the flying-fish blueprint): genomic (Ensembl, NCBI Gene, ZFIN alleles and mutant phenotypes with ZFA anatomy, Alliance orthology and disease), transcriptomic, proteomic, pathway and PTM, grouped by feature with per-entry concordance (n_sources) and listed conflicts. Accepts a ZFIN symbol, a ZFIN gene id, or a human orthologue symbol.

symbol.description: ZFIN symbol (e.g. kcnk5b), ZDB-GENE id, or human orthologue symbol (e.g. KCNK5).

tools.name: omics_part
tools.title: Genes recorded at a blueprint part, with multi-omic summaries
tools.description: Genes with an omics row whose anatomy (or cell type) is this part: an UBERON or CL id from the flying-fish blueprint (UBERON:0000151 = pectoral fin), or a ZFA id mapped through the ontology crosswalk. Direct records only, no propagation from sub-parts. Each gene comes with the layers that place it there, row counts per feature, and its per-layer row totals.

layer.description: Only genes placed at the part by this layer.

tools.name: omics_search
tools.title: Search omics annotations by feature value or term
tools.description: Find genes whose omics rows mention a term: an anatomy label, a GO/Reactome/KEGG/WikiPathways/InterPro/Pfam/DOID id or label, a phenotype phrase, a modification. Substring match on normalised values; returns matching terms with their layers, features and genes.

feature.description: Restrict to one feature (e.g. allele_phenotype, pathway_member).

tools.name: closest_relative_phenotype
tools.title: Closest real relative (phenotype)
tools.description: Embed the design's resolved STATE (SL, mass/SL^3, depth/SL, width/SL, peduncle fractions, fin sizes) and return the nearest real organisms/specimens with distance, dominant features and an out-of-distribution flag whose threshold is calibrated on held-out real specimens.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (zebrafish-adult, flying-fish, winged-zebrafish, tff, ff-zf-chimera, ...), or an inline organism document. Gene edits: target {level:"gene", id}, param "allele" with an HGVS-like value (p.W169L, p.Y285*, c.505del, p.T200K/+), "knockout" or "expression_fold"; genes outside the vetted map go in doc.genotype [{gene, change}].

specimen.description: Instead of an organism: a raw specimen record {SL_m, mass_kg, depth_SL, width_SL, ped_depth_frac, ped_width_frac, pectoral_len_SL, ...} (e.g. a museum specimen).

exclude.description: Reference ids or groups to leave out of the nearest-neighbour search (e.g. "organism:zebrafish" for a leave-lineage-out check).

tools.name: closest_relative_genotype
tools.title: Closest real relative (genotype)
tools.description: For each gene-level edit, compare the edited protein against real orthologues (sequences/alignments first; NCBI BLAST on request): % identity, closest species, and whether the edited residue state exists in any real organism or known allele. A residue is a STATE, not a phenotype: nothing here predicts a phenotype.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (zebrafish-adult, flying-fish, winged-zebrafish, tff, ff-zf-chimera, ...), or an inline organism document. Gene edits: target {level:"gene", id}, param "allele" with an HGVS-like value (p.W169L, p.Y285*, c.505del, p.T200K/+), "knockout" or "expression_fold"; genes outside the vetted map go in doc.genotype [{gene, change}].

network.description: Allow cached network calls (UniProt, Ensembl). Default true; results are cached in sim-engine/validate/cache/.

blast.description: For genes not in sequences/alignments: run NCBI BLAST (blastp nr, NOT Aves[Organism]; minutes; cached). Default false.

tools.name: sanity_check_design
tools.title: Genotype and phenotype sanity checks
tools.description: Genotype: reference residue, frame, premature stop, conserved site, annotated domain, causal-chain caveats. Phenotype: allometry within the range observed across 16 377 FishShapes specimens, mass fits the body envelope, flight muscle fits (mesh or analytic), partedit containment if supplied, stage consistency. Each check: passed / failed / flagged / could-not-run.

tools.name: parse_design_text
tools.title: Parse a design request (plain English) into a DesignSpec
tools.description: Deterministic, rule-based parser (no LLM). Returns the DesignSpec it could read, every piece of text it could NOT read (`unparsed`, verbatim, with the reason), requests it refused (`refused`: birds are a frozen holdout; Lean laws cannot be waived), every default it applied (`assumptions`), and the spec validated against the engine (`validation`). An agent should resolve every unparsed item with the user before calling design_from_spec.

text.description: The request, e.g. "a zebrafish that glides at least 30 m from 1 m, survives 4 °C to 32 °C, outswims a 0.3 m/s current as a larva and adult".

tools.name: design_from_spec
tools.title: Design an organism that meets a functional spec
tools.description: Validates the DesignSpec against the engine (unknown scenarios, metrics, units, parts and params are rejected with the reason), evaluates the starting design on every criterion at every requested stage, runs the `optimize` tool over the editable parameters with the hard criteria as constraints and the Lean laws holding, then explains the result per criterion and per stage: met / failed / no-model, with the limiting factor and the weakest provenance kind behind each verdict. A design "meets the spec" only if every hard criterion holds at every requested stage and no Lean law is violated; a criterion with no model counts as NOT met.

organism.description: zebrafish-adult, zebrafish-larva, flying-fish, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera

start_from.description: Parents and weights; weights sum to 1. Birds are refused (frozen holdout).

base_edits.description: Optional organism.mjs edits applied before optimizing: {target:{level,id}, param, op:"set"|"scale"|"add", value}.

params.description: Scenario parameters (aliases such as water_temp_C or pressure_kPa are mapped and converted; the result says so).

metric.description: A metric key the scenario declares. Not needed for op "survives".

op.description: survives = the organism lives (run().survives); feasible = the behaviour is possible (run().feasible: can glide, hold station, grip, escape).

stages.description: 'all', a list of embryo/larva/juvenile/adult, or {ageDays:{min,max}} (days after hatching). Default ['adult'].

hard.description: Default: true for >=, <=, survives; false (and must be) for maximize/minimize.

editable.description: Decision variables. Use organism_list_parts for valid targets and params.

text.description: Alternative to spec: parsed with parse_design_text first; refused or unparsed text stops the run.

strict.description: Reject ANY binding Lean violation, including ones the unedited parents already have (default: reject only NEW ones, as optimize does).

evaluate_only.description: Skip the optimizer: validate and explain the starting design only.

Leases default to 600 s.

target.description: What the task works on (a part id, a scenario, a proposal id...).

inputs.description: Data the worker needs. Data, not instructions.

posted_by_role.description: Your agent role label, e.g. 'agent:organ-gen-1'. Never a name, e-mail or handle.

tools.name: swarm_claim
tools.title: Claim a task under a lease
tools.description: Claims the first claimable task matching your role (or task_id), under a lease. A role holds one live claim at a time; claiming again returns it. Expired leases are claimable by anyone matching. renew:true extends your lease. Returns the task, the session organism and the other agents' proposals and comments.

role.description: Your agent role label, e.g. 'agent:organ-gen-1'. Never a name, e-mail or handle.

tools.name: swarm_submit
tools.title: Submit a task result
tools.description: Finishes your claimed task. outcome 'done' with edits posts a session PROPOSAL (validated, not applied; a human decides); without edits it posts a COMMENT carrying summary + findings. outcome 'failed' posts a comment and frees the task for another attempt (until max_attempts).

role.description: Your agent role label, e.g. 'agent:organ-gen-1'. Never a name, e-mail or handle.

tools.name: swarm_status

tools.description: Applies edits to an inline copy of the session organism (nothing saved) and returns per-edit Lean verdicts and edit_effect, plus optional scenario runs [{scenario, params, ageDays}]. Use it before submitting a proposal.

role.description: Your agent role label, e.g. 'agent:organ-gen-1'. Never a name, e-mail or handle.

tools.name: generate_candidates
tools.title: Generate candidate designs (flow matching / diffusion)
tools.description: Generate n candidate organisms (body level: a conditional flow-matching or DDPM model trained on 16 123 real teleost specimens from FishShapes v1, returning body parameters AND ready-to-use organism documents) or protein designs (NVIDIA NIM ProteinMPNN/RFdiffusion/Evo2 when NVIDIA_API_KEY works; otherwise a public structure fallback and no generation). Organ, system, tissue and cell levels return "no training data" / "not configured" with the reason. Every candidate carries provenance; generated values are kind "assumed". Feed a candidate's `organism` to organism_get, scenario_run or optimize (organism accepts a document) to test or refine it.

level.description: Which level to generate at. Only body (local) and protein (NVIDIA NIM, if keyed) can generate; the others return their honest status.

base.description: body: organism id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, a design id), a parent list [{organism, weight}], or an organism document. protein: a UniProt accession or amino-acid sequence (DNA for mode dna).

text.description: How to augment, in words: "a flying fish with a much deeper body", "slightly more slender, heavier", "tuna-like". Fin and organ words are reported as not generated.

conditions.description: body: {model: fm|ddpm, keep_size (default true), shape_family, sd_shift: {depth|width|peduncle_depth|peduncle_width|condition_K|SL|head_depth: k}, observe: {body_depth_over_SL: 0.25, ...}, steps, llm_assist: nebius|vertex}. protein: {mode: inverse_fold|design|dna, contigs, temperature, num_tokens}.

seed.description: Sampling seed (default 1); same seed and inputs give the same candidates.

tools.name: generative_backends_status
tools.title: Generative backends: what is real, configured, reachable
tools.description: Per level (body, protein, organ, system, tissue, cell) and per provider (NVIDIA NIM, Nebius AI Studio, Google Vertex AI, public AlphaFold DB / ESM Atlas): ok, not configured, auth failed, unreachable, or no training data. Keys are read from the environment only and never returned. Includes the body model's held-out metrics.

tools.name: validate_generation
tools.title: Validate a generated organism against the desired phenotype, at every scale
tools.description:
The unifying design validator. Input: the generated organism, the base organism, and the DESIRED PHENOTYPE AS TEXT (the same prompt the generator was given). It parses the text into a DesignSpec, identifies the closest FUNCTIONAL analogue from the desired function rather than from relatedness and fetches that analogue's genotype, sweeps the functional annotations at every biological scale (sequence/genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, PTM, pathway, then cell, tissue, organ, organ system, body), then runs functional_resolution, lean_check and physics_check with the spec as the physics target.

Returns five named results side by side, each with its own gate, NEVER summed, plus a per-scale coverage number and a verdict SENTENCE naming what passed, what failed and what could not be assessed.

Be clear about the sequence limit before reading the output: this project has no generated whole genomes. A design is its base plus edits, so when a document or design id is supplied the generated sequence is reconstructed AT THE EDITED LOCI ONLY, and when the design carries no gene-level edit (the usual case) nothing is reconstructed at all. 'sequence_basis' and 'loci_covered' say which of the three cases applies on every call. Any unparsed part of the desired-phenotype text is returned verbatim: an unparsed requirement is an unchecked requirement.

A validation REPORT, not a validity claim. Five named results are reported side by side with their own gates and are never summed; a composite score, if the scorer produced one, is carried through as the scorer's own number and is not this report's verdict. Every annotation in the multi-scale sweep is a proxy-species record (zebrafish, medaka, Mexican tetra) or an annotation borrowed from a human or mouse orthologue: none is a measurement of the designed organism and none is a measurement of the flying fish. Absence of a record means "not recorded", never "not present". Birds (Aves) are a frozen holdout and appear in no reference set, no analogue and no annotation. MORPHOLOGICAL designs are shapes, not organisms: a parameter delta is not an allele, a pathway or a developmental programme.

desired_phenotype.description: The desired phenotype as free text -- the same prompt the generator was given. Parsed by lib/parse-text.mjs; whatever cannot be parsed is returned verbatim and marked unchecked.

generated.description: The generated organism: a design id (e.g. "winged-zebrafish"), an inline organism document, a path to an organism-document JSON, or a path to / string of FASTA or plain sequence.

base.description: The base organism, in any of the same forms (e.g. "zebrafish-adult").

network.description: Allow network lookups (Ensembl, used only to reconstruct sequence at edited loci). Default false.

lawset.description: Lean lawset version for the Lean check. Default "current".

ageDays.description: Evaluate at this age in days instead of the criterion's stages.

conditions.description: Ambient conditions override (see conditions/baseline.json for what is otherwise held fixed).

reference_set_excluding.description: Leave-out entries for the phenotype reference set (ids, "species:", "family:", "order:", "organism:").

extra_genes.description: Extra gene symbols to include in the multi-scale sweep beyond the focal panel and the edited genes.

tools.name: functional_resolution
tools.title: Functional-analogue ledger: how each difference is accounted for
tools.description: The FOURTH named result, beside genotype_similarity, phenotype_similarity, lean_check and physics_check. It picks the closest FUNCTIONAL analogue from the DESIRED FUNCTION (which real animal is recorded as doing the thing that was asked for) rather than from relatedness or shape, derives that analogue's requirement set, and then classifies every difference between the design and the analogue on a six-rung ladder: SAME > ALLELIC > PARALOGUE > ANALOGOUS_SET > COMPENSATORY > UNRESOLVED. DEMONSTRATED resolutions (SAME, ALLELIC, PARALOGUE, ANALOGOUS_SET) and HYPOTHESISED ones (COMPENSATORY) are reported apart and are NEVER summed: "this gap could be compensated" is a claim about an unobserved mechanism, not a resolution. An UNRESOLVED difference is a GATE failure: the design is not functionally accounted for, whatever the similarity scores say. Nothing here moves the composite design score. Read `coverage` before quoting any count. Coverage is partial (roughly 30 % of requirements are assessable on the headline case) and the analogue itself is data-poor: there is no flying-fish expression or functional-assay data at any locus, so `functional_data_we_hold` is the honest denominator, not the ledger length. Supply `desired_phenotype` whenever you have it: with no desired function the analogue is INFERRED from the design's declared identity and the result says so.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (zebrafish-adult, flying-fish, winged-zebrafish, tff, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera, ...), or an inline organism document.

desired_phenotype.description: The desired phenotype / function as free text -- the same prompt the generator was given. It is the signal that chooses the analogue. Omit it and the function is inferred from the design's identity, and the ledger says it was inferred.

spec.description: A DesignSpec instead of (or beside) the text; its criteria are also read for the function. Build one with parse_design_text.

pectoral_len_over_SL.description: The design's pectoral fin length as a fraction of SL, for the functional half of the analogue distance, when the document does not carry it.

network.description: Allow cached network lookups. Default false; the ledger answers from shipped data and cache.

tools.name: physics_check
tools.title: Does the design actually do the thing? (physics simulation)
tools.description: The FIFTH named result, beside genotype_similarity, phenotype_similarity, lean_check and functional_resolution. Runs the engine's own scenario modules on the design at every requested life stage and reports, per criterion of the desired function, met / not met / NO MODEL, with the measured metric, the threshold and the limiting factor. KEEP THE DISTINCTION: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW (necessary, never sufficient); this says the design ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. The target function comes from `spec` (a DesignSpec) when given and is then authoritative; with no spec it is inferred from the design's declared intent and said to be inferred. Also runs the standing physical checks for the organism as separate NAMED checks (can it reach its own v_min, does its lifting area support its mass, does drag power fit the aerobic ceiling, does the organ volume fit the body, is it stable in pitch) -- never folded into one number. Every check carries a model_confidence stating whether the model behind it is independently validated, rests on assumed inputs, or is CIRCULAR (scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with); "function achieved" is never reported without it. Where the inputs have a spread, a seeded ensemble over the stated distributions reports the FRACTION of draws in which the function is achieved plus the median and the 5-95 % band: a design that achieves its function in 8 % of draws has not achieved it. A criterion no scenario can model comes back as `no model` and is listed under unchecked_requirements; it is never dropped and never counts as met. It is a GATE, not a score: physics_gate_failed is true when a hard criterion is not met, and nothing here moves the composite score.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (flying-fish, zebrafish-adult, tff, winged-zebrafish, wingless-flying-fish, ff-zf-chimera, ...), or an inline organism document.

specimen.description: Instead of an organism: a raw specimen record. A specimen has no STATE, so no scenario can be run on it and the result is `ran: false` with the reason.

spec.description: A DesignSpec (lib/spec.mjs): {start_from, base_edits, criteria:[{scenario, params, metric, op, value, unit, stages, hard, weight, source_text}]}. AUTHORITATIVE when given: that IS the desired function. Build one from a text prompt with parse_design_text.

ageDays.description: Pin every criterion to one age instead of its declared stages.

conditions.description: Ambient conditions passed to resolveState (depth_m, altitude_m, temperature_C, headwind_m_s, ...).

draws.description: Ensemble draws per criterion per stage (default 200). 0 switches the ensemble off, and then no fraction-of-draws figure is reported.

seed.description: Ensemble seed (default 'delphi-v1'). The same seed gives the same ensemble.

ensemble.description: false switches the ensemble off (same as draws: 0).

launch_height_m.description: Launch height for the standing flight checks (default 1 m, the glide scenario's own default; kind assumed).

tools.name: flight_support_check
tools.title: Do the wings carry the animal? (any clade, from declared inputs)
tools.description: The one aerodynamic question, asked of ANY animal: does lift at the stated airspeed carry the stated weight? L = 1/2 rho v^2 S C_L >= m g. Nothing in that is clade-specific except C_L, which is a property of a particular wing and is taken by clade from a named measurement (sim-engine/validate/physics/lift-coefficients.json) -- never defaulted. No sourced coefficient for the clade means NO NUMBER, because the alternative is answering a question about a mouse with a flying fish lift curve. Use this where physics_check refuses: physics_check runs scenario modules over a resolved STATE and the engine holds body-plan parameters for its own teleosts only, so for any other animal it stops before reaching the aerodynamics. EVERY quantity must arrive with a source; a bare number is refused by name, and a range is swept so the verdict covers it. It is a STEADY-STATE AREA CHECK: it cannot answer powered flight (a power question, not an area question) and says so when asked, and it models no control, no stability and no ability to reach the speed in the first place.

taxon.description: The animal this is about (scientific name or a clade the clade table knows). Decides the lift coefficient; without it there is no coefficient and no answer.

mass_kg.description: Body mass. A quantity WITH ITS SOURCE: {value, source} or {min, max, source} for a range, which is swept. A bare number is refused.

lifting_area_m2.description: The area that generates lift, measured the same way the coefficient is referred to. A quantity WITH ITS SOURCE: {value, source} or {min, max, source} for a range, which is swept. A bare number is refused.

airspeed_m_s.description: The airspeed at which it is asked to be flying. A quantity WITH ITS SOURCE: {value, source} or {min, max, source} for a range, which is swept. A bare number is refused.

air_density_kg_m3.description: Optional {value, source}. ISA sea level (1.225 kg/m3) if omitted, and the result says it was not supplied.

powered.description: true if the question is about POWERED flight. The check then refuses and says what a power answer would need, rather than returning an area result to a power question.

question.description: The question as asked, in words. Only read for whether it is about powered flight.

tools.name: edit_plan
tools.title: Germline editing plan for a design's gene edits (proposal, not a protocol)
tools.description: For each gene-level edit on a design, the concrete zebrafish germline editing plan: the exact GRCz11 coordinates of the change (gene -> canonical transcript -> CDS -> codon -> chromosome position, with the reference codon CHECKED against the genome), SpCas9/SaCas9/Cas12a protospacers in the required window with their cut sites, a full ssODN donor with homology arms and silent PAM/seed blocking mutations, a base-editor route where the change is a transition and a designed pegRNA where it is a transversion, an off-target search against GRCz11 with the gene context of every close mismatched site, an `evo2` block that RANKS the edit and its silent blocking mutations by Evo2 (NVIDIA NIM / BioNeMo) sequence likelihood, a `ranking` section holding every order the plan computes with the rule behind each, and - as first-class output - what is NOT established, plus a "what would falsify this plan" section. Every number is labelled. There are TWO on-target scores and the difference matters: `on_target_doench2014` is a PUBLISHED model (Doench 2014 Rule Set 1, coefficients fetched from the paper and self-tested) fitted in mouse and human cells, so applying it to zebrafish is a cross-species transfer; `on_target` is OUR heuristic with weights we chose. Neither is Doench 2016 Rule Set 2, which cannot be reimplemented from published numbers. The off-target search is an EXHAUSTIVE local scan of the GRCz11 primary assembly - complete for substitutions, but blind to bulges, to alternative loci and to the laboratory strain's own genome. Evo2 likelihoods RANK and never gate, and are NOT phenotype predictions. HDR rates are other papers' loci. Danio rerio only: it refuses every other species, and will not produce a human or other mammalian plan.

organism.description: Organism: a saved document id, a repository organism/design id (winged-zebrafish, flying-fish, ...), or an inline organism document. Its gene-level edits are each turned into an editing plan. Use `gene` + `change` instead to plan one edit directly.

gene.description: Zebrafish gene symbol (resolved through Ensembl; an unresolvable symbol is a refusal, not a guess). Use with `change`.

change.description: The edit: a protein change "p.W169L" / "p.Y285*", or "knockout". Anything else is refused rather than guessed at.

species.description: Must be danio_rerio (the default). Any other value is refused: this tool does not plan human or other mammalian edits.

window.description: For a point change: the cut site must be within this many bp of the edited codon (default 30). Cut-site proximity is the main lever on knock-in efficiency (Prykhozhij 2018).

arms.description: ssODN homology-arm style. Default: both (40/40 and the asymmetric variant).

offtarget.description: Run the GRCz11 off-target search. Default true. By default this is a LOCAL EXHAUSTIVE scan of the whole GRCz11 primary assembly (~22 s per guide, cached) which is complete for substitutions at or under 4 mismatches. Set false for a fast structural answer; the plan then says the search did not run, and absence of listed off-targets is NOT evidence of specificity.

offtarget_method.description: Off-target backend. "auto" (default) uses the local exhaustive index if it is built, else NCBI BLAST. "local" requires the index (build once: node sim-engine/validate/editplan/grcz11-local.mjs build). "ncbi" forces the NCBI BLAST URL API, which is a heuristic aligner and which did not return at all in our runs (see edit_plan_methods off_target.ncbi_blast).

offtarget_guides.description: How many guides to search (default 3). The local search is cheap enough to search every guide a lab would weigh against the others.

evo2.description: Build the Evo2 (NVIDIA NIM / BioNeMo) block, which RANKS candidate edits and silent blocking mutations by sequence likelihood. Default true. With no NVIDIA_API_KEY every Evo2 field is {ran:false, reason} and the plan is complete without it: the model never gates anything. A likelihood is NOT a phenotype prediction and NOT evidence of safety or specificity.

network.description: Allow network calls (Ensembl REST, Kazusa, and the off-target backend). Default true. Everything is cached under C:/Temp/editplan-cache (EDITPLAN_CACHE_DIR). No credentials are used; the Evo2 key, if present, is read from the environment only and never written anywhere.

panel_only.description: Return just the validation-report panel section, not the full plans.

tools.name: edit_plan_methods
tools.title: How edit_plan computes every number, and what each number is not
tools.description: The scoring rules, the off-target search, the reagent precedents, the feasibility statements with their citations, and the falsifier list - without running a plan. Read this before quoting any number edit_plan produced.

tools.name: lean_open_questions
tools.title: List open questions and failed theorems
tools.description: Everything this project holds UNSETTLED (open questions, each with its arms and a computed belief proportion) and everything it tried and could not establish (failed theorems, each with its reason and what survives). Filter by status, by whether an arm is formalised in Lean, by a law_id or design property the question touches, or by free text.

status.description: One status or a list. Default: all.

formalised.description: true: only questions with at least one arm formalised in Lean.

touches.description: A law_id, constraint id, design property or scenario key the question bears on, e.g. "perturb-depth-cap", "adult_mass", "sleep".

text.description: Substring of question_id, statement or an arm statement.

include_failed.description: Include failed theorems and requirement records. Default true.

tools.name: lean_open_question
tools.title: Get one open question, failed theorem or requirement record
tools.description: One full record: every arm with its position, its Lean reference where it has been formalised, its evidence with VERBATIM quotes and locators, its computed belief and the breakdown behind it; whether the arms actually contradict; what would settle the question and whether that is feasible today; and what in this project rests on the answer. Accepts a question_id (oq-*), failure_id (ft-*) or requirement_id (cr-*).

id.description: question_id (oq-*, e.g. "oq-kcnk5b-vm-sign"), failure_id (ft-*, e.g. "ft-glider-interface-convergence"), requirement_id (cr-*) or not_checkable_id (nc-*, e.g. "nc-hamilton-rule").

recompute.description: Recompute the belief proportion from the arms' evidence and return it alongside the stored one, so a caller can verify the number rather than trust it.

tools.name: lean_open_question_guard
tools.title: Would this law be refused for asserting an open arm?
tools.description: Run the open-question guard against a proposed law WITHOUT writing anything. Returns the arms it would be found to assert, and the full refusal text naming the question, its arms, the computed proportion and what would settle it. Ask this before writing the Lean, not after.

statement_en.description: The law's plain-English statement, as it would be written.

lean_theorem.description: Fully qualified theorem name, if there is one.

lean_structure.description: Fully qualified hypothesis structure name, if there is one.

hypotheses.description: As the law file would carry them.
